aspects.fertilizer:
General fertilizer requirements:
Guar is a leguminous crop.
It does not require much fertilizer.

Fertilizer dose and timing:
Apply one bag of DAP per acre at the time of sowing.
Apply half a bag of Urea per acre at flowering.
Applying these amounts produces a good yield.

DAP application method:
Mix DAP into the soil by broadcasting during land preparation to achieve good results.
Applying DAP after sowing provides no significant benefit.
aspects.harvesting:
**Seed crop harvesting:**
Harvest the seed crop when 80 to 90 percent of the pods are ripe.
Dry the harvested crop for some time in small heaps.
Extract the seeds using a wheat thresher.
Dry the seeds thoroughly in the sun for 1 to 2 days before storing them.

**Threshing method:**
Threshing guar directly can be slow, consume excessive diesel, waste time, and crush grains inside the thresher.
After harvesting, engage the right gear to run rotor blades and separate the stems from the pods.
Pass only the pods through the thresher.
This method saves diesel, saves time, and produces clean seed.

**Fodder crop harvesting:**
Harvest the fodder crop within 45 to 60 days.
Harvest when the crop reaches a suitable height.
Harvest before flowers and pods form.

**Canal-irrigated areas:**
Green fodder yield is 250 to 300 maunds per acre.

**Rain-fed barani areas:**
Green fodder yield is 150 to 200 maunds per acre.
aspects.irrigation:
General:
The guar crop has a considerable ability to tolerate water shortage.
Irrigation at the appropriate time results in good yield.
Less irrigation is needed in the event of rainfall.

Rain-fed areas:
Irrigation relies entirely on rainfall.

Canal-irrigated areas:
Applying water three times is essential to achieve good yield.
The first irrigation should be given 1 to 1.5 months after germination.
The second irrigation should be given at flowering.
The third irrigation should be given at pod formation.

Water drainage:
If rainwater stands in the field, drain it out immediately.
Plants die if standing rainwater is not drained immediately.
aspects.machinery:
Land preparation:
Level land is very essential for better germination.
Plough the field 2 to 3 times and run a planker.
This makes the soil soft and crumbly.
It improves aeration for the crop roots and produces good yield.

Sowing machinery:
There is currently no specific drill available for planting guar in rows.
A wheat drill can be successfully used for row cultivation.
Close one hole and keep the other hole open on the wheat drill.
This maintains a distance of 1.5 feet between rows.
Row planting makes hoeing, weed control, and pest spraying easy.
Broadcasting makes hoeing, weed control, and spraying difficult to perform.

Threshing machinery:
Slow threshing wastes time and increases diesel expenses.
Slow threshing can also crush and damage the grains inside the thresher.
After harvesting the crop, engage the right gear and run rotor blades.
This separates the stems from the pods.
Pass only the pods through the thresher.
This practice saves diesel and time.
It also yields clean seed.

aspects.overview:
Overview:
Guar, also called cluster bean, is a leguminous crop cultivated for centuries in the Indo-Pak subcontinent.
About 95 percent of the world guar is produced in the Indo-Pak subcontinent.
Its native habitat is arid and semi-arid.
It contains up to 35 percent of a component that increases animal meat.
It is grown with little labor and low cost in low-water areas.
Guar fixes 300 pounds of atmospheric nitrogen per acre into the soil in one season.

Cultivation regions:
In Punjab, guar is cultivated mainly in Mianwali, Sargodha, Bhakkar, Jhang, Khushab, Layyah, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, and Rahim Yar Khan districts.
In Sindh, it is cultivated in dry areas.

Soil and climate:
Guar requires a hot and dry climate.
The plant tolerates severe heat and drought but cannot tolerate excess water.
Sandy loam soil with good drainage is suitable.
It can be grown in all soils except saline soils.
Its roots grow deep into the soil.

Approved varieties:
Agriculture Research Station Bahawalpur developed three approved varieties: BR-90, BR-99, and BR-2017.
BR-2017 is a new cluster-type variety with broad, shiny leaves and tall stature.

Uses:
Guar is used as grain, green fodder, green manure, and vegetable.
It is used in food and paper industries.
Guar gum from the seed is used in ice cream, jelly, cosmetics, tobacco, gunpowder, chilies, fish and animal feed, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and oil industries.
Large quantities of guar gum are used in drilling wells for shale gas exploration in the United States.
It is used in medicine for patients with heart disease, diabetes, and asthma.

Production metrics:
Clean seed is 220 kilograms per acre.
At 1.5 feet row spacing, there are 147 rows per acre.
There are 396 seeded pods in 198 feet of row length.
Total plant population per acre is approximately 58,000 plants.
Average number of pods per plant is 150.
Average number of grains per pod is 8.
A single plant yields 1,200 grains.
Average weight of 100 grains is 35 grams.
Average weight of 1,200 grains per plant is 42 grams.
Total production from 58,000 plants is 2,436 kilograms.
Modern production technology yields 60.9 maunds per acre.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Pests:
Caterpillars do not attack the guar crop.
Sucking pests attack guar, including whitefly, green jassid, thrips, and aphids.
Apply sprays for pest control with the advice of agriculture department staff.

Diseases:
Wilt disease is sometimes observed in this crop.
Wilt can be treated by spraying with Trichoderma.
Diseases can be controlled on this crop by using fungicides.
Treating seeds with fungicides before sowing controls diseases to a great extent.

Spray Precautions:
Strictly avoid hoeing the crop immediately after spraying.
Hoeing right after spraying breaks the poison effect and weeds can regrow.
Hoeing causes dust to fly, which can cause the chemical to enter the farmer's body and breath, severely damaging health.
aspects.sowing:
Sowing Times:
Guar for fodder is best sown from April to July.
Guar for seed is best sown from the start of June to the end of July.
Guar for green manure should be sown in May.

Thal and Rain-fed Areas:
Guar is generally sown by the end of July upon the arrival of rains.

Sowing Methods:
Guar is sown by drill or by broadcasting.
For a seed crop, drilling in rows or sowing behind the plough gives the best results.
Always sow seeds in moist soil to improve germination.

Spacing and Density:
Plant to plant distance is 6 inches.
Plant density is 58,000 to 60,000 plants per acre for best yield.
An acre measuring 220 feet in length has 147 rows at a 1.5-foot row distance.
A row measuring 198 feet in length has 396 plants at a 6-inch plant distance.

Row Drilling:
There is no specific drill for row sowing of guar.
A wheat drill can be used by closing one hole and keeping the next open.
This wheat drill method sows rows at a distance of 1.5 feet.
Row drilling facilitates hoeing, weed control, and insect pest spraying.
Broadcasting makes hoeing, weed control, and spraying difficult.

Irrigated, High Rainfall, and Hard Soil Areas:
Guar can be sown on ridges to make water drainage easy during rains.
Construct ridges 1.5 feet wide.
Apply water and then dibble seeds by hand on both sides of the ridges at 6 inches distance.
Ridge sowing requires 5 to 6 kg of seed per acre instead of 10 kg.
Weed issues can occur on ridges and are controlled using suitable weed-killing sprays.
aspects.varieties:
Seed Rate:
For green manure and fodder crops, the seed rate is 20 to 25 kg per acre.
For seed crops, the seed rate is 8 to 10 kg per acre.
Seed must be viable, pure, healthy, plump, and have proper germination capacity.

Sowing Method:
Soak seed in water for 1.0 to 1.5 hours and dry in the shade before sowing for faster germination.

Irrigated, High Rainfall, and Hard Soil Areas:
Guar can be sown on ridges to allow easy water drainage during rain.
Make ridges 1.5 feet wide and apply water.
Dibble seeds by hand on both sides of the ridges at a spacing of 6 inches.
Ridge sowing requires 5 to 6 kg seed per acre instead of 10 kg.
Weeds can be a problem with this method and should be controlled with suitable herbicide sprays.

Disease Management:
Drying or wilt disease sometimes appears in the crop.
The disease can be sprayed using Trichoderma.
Fungicide sprays can be used to control crop diseases.
Treating seeds with fungicides before sowing controls diseases significantly.

Approved Varieties:
Agriculture Research Station Bahawalpur developed three approved varieties: BR-90, BR-99, and BR-2017.
BR-2017 is a new and superior variety.
BR-2017 is a cluster type with broad, shiny leaves and tall plant height.
The research station focuses on varieties that tolerate water scarcity, resist diseases and insect pests, yield high guar gum content, and produce high yields.

Yield Metrics:
The number of seeds obtained from one plant is 1200.
The average weight of 100 seeds is 35 grams.
The average weight of 1200 seeds per plant is 42 grams.
aspects.weeds:
Chemical Weed Control:
Apply weedicide before plowing when the soil reaches moisture condition.
Mix Pendimethalin at a rate of 1.5 liters per acre in 100 liters of water.
This spray eliminates weeds.
When cultivating on ridges, spray weedicide after sowing for effective weed control.

Irrigated, High Rainfall, and Hard Soil Areas:
Guar can be cultivated on ridges in irrigated areas, high rainfall areas, and hard soil areas.
Ridge cultivation facilitates easy water drainage in case of rain.
Make ridges 1.5 feet wide.
Apply water to the ridges first.
Hand-dibble seeds on both sides of the ridges at a spacing of 6 inches.
This ridge method requires 5 to 6 kilograms of seed instead of 10 kilograms.
Ridge cultivation can face weed problems.
Control weeds in ridge cultivation using an appropriate weedicide spray.

Post-Spraying Precautions:
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after spraying.
Hoeing immediately breaks the chemical effect and allows weeds to regrow.
Hoeing causes dust to rise, which enters the farmer body and breath, causing severe health damage.
